newsitem.title: USA: Cameroon must act on taxes, oil income for IMF loan.
newsitem.headline: Cameroon must act on taxes, oil income for IMF loan.

text.p: A planned International Monetary Fund loan to Cameroon will require government action on taxes, oil revenues and structural reform, an international monetary source said on Wednesday.

The source, who asked not to be identified, said the three-year Enhanced Structural Adjustment Facility would be discussed soon by the IMF board, but an IMF team had already recommended that it be approved.
He said Cameroon would be entitled to borrow a total of 160 million special drawing rights -- or about $215 million -- provided it met IMF conditions.

Cameroon Finance Minister Edouard Akame Mfoumou said last week that the loan, which he put at $125 million plus 20 billion CFA francs ($32 million), would be signed on August 20. Cameroon would receive an initial payment of 22 billion CFA francs, he said.
Cameroon has had four short-term IMF standby arrangements in the past, but they lapsed after agreed policies were not maintained.
